shared_elements: quadruped animal shown in profile with elongated body and tail
shallow low-relief carving on a flat dressed stone face
weathered limestone slab/pillar with a raised framing edge
simplified silhouette forms without interior detail
excavated stone rubble context around the carved block
justification: Both are pale weathered stone slabs carved in very shallow relief with simplified profile quadrupeds rendered as flat silhouettes, and both animals share the same convention of a long body with a sweeping, tapering tail. The decisive difference is density and organisation: A carries a single isolated creature on a largely empty field, whereas B is a crowded multi-register composition with a row of arch-topped motifs, a fringed band, a disc and human-like figures, so the compositional schemes have almost nothing in common.
